chapter: Band family, war years and wrap-up
title: Aunt Lee in Newark
summary: His aunt looked after his schooling and brought sweet potato pie.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And my aunt told me not to go to Chicago. If you're going anywhere, you're coming to New York. You know? And then if things don't go right, I can look out for you.
I'd go out on a tour with my band. My aunt was working for a doctor on Mt. Pleasant Street in Newark. He was there for years. And she had been there for years, and she had

looked out for me in school cause, you know, at the time my mother wasn't able to cause I was fatherless. And, I was older. So, my aunt took it upon herself, you know, to see that I'd get some schooling.

And, she used to send me some spending money. But, I'd never, never asked her for it. She'd just send me some. The school was doing all right with me. Like the president would give me 1 or 2 dollars if I needed it for a show. You know? And then, the band would go out. Then, I was satisfied.

So, when I came to New York, if I was on a tour. Okay. When I came back off that tour, she would call me up at my house. She'd say come over here. I want the doctor to examine you. You're gonna be sure that I get examined everytime that I go over there and come back. That's how close she was to me.
And the doctor, after so many times, the doctor said there ain't nothing wrong with this boy. So he said well, I could look at him anyhow. I'll be satisfied. You
know, she just passed on a few years ago.

Then for, when I left school, my sister went to the same school. So, she told me now look at for your sister in school. So, I did the same things for my sister that she did for me. You know, until she finished.
She taught school for awhile in Birmingham before she married then settled down.
My wife here just sent her a big package to say hello, just to say hello. So, they're doing all right.

I had some good years. There I'm thinking about how my aunt felt towards me. She used to come over to the Savoy Ballroom every Sunday when I'm playing a matinee. She knew I liked sweet potato pie. I love sweets. I guess that's the reason why I'm so heavy.
You know, she'd make one there and bring it on the sub, all the way to New York, so that I could have my pie, my sweet potato pie. And when I was in town, when I was at the
Savoy, I'd have a matinee at 4:00. She was there. And then I'd go over and see her now and then. Aunt Lee, I called her. Aunt Lee, my mother's older sister.
